intro: Switch sides. You run lab_30, and chip-30 seals whatever you plan.

workbench.security_note: Only these two chips' keys may exist in the client. Never ship the level chips' keys or ROT_SEED.

part_a.title: Certify
part_a.prompt: Plan a training job of at least {min_flops} FLOPs that passes. In three sentences, say why each check passes.

starting_state._notes: Each student gets values drawn from these ranges. check_content.py confirms the worst case is still solvable.

part_a.worked_example: lab_30 has used 1.72 × 10¹² FLOPs and 3.40 kJ, and chip-30's last counter is 6. At 0.5 × 10¹² FLOPs, energy must sit between 0.745 kJ (the training band's upper edge plus 10%) and 0.97 kJ (the noise-adjusted energy cap).

rubric.criterion: The FLOP and energy cap arithmetic is shown

part_b.title: Forge
part_b.prompt: Build four forgeries, each aimed at a different check. Predict what catches each one.

forgeries.build: Change a value inside a sealed envelope
Seal a report with the unregistered chip
Resubmit one of your earlier sealed records
Two jobs that each pass alone but together cross a cap

forgeries.note: Passes if the ratio sits in the overlap of the two bands.

part_b.scoring: 1 point for each correct prediction and 1 for each sound explanation, best four forgeries.

part_c.title: The one that gets through
part_c.prompt: Build a dishonest record that passes. Why did nothing catch it? Suggest one defence.
known_exploits: A training run labelled inference, with a ratio inside the overlap of the two bands (376–610 × 10⁹ FLOPs per kJ). It escapes the FLOP cap.
Work the FLOP meter misses, kept small enough that the energy stays inside the band.
A job run on another lab's chip. The bouncer charges the chip's owner, not whoever actually ran the job.

rubric.criterion: The explanation names which check's blind spot it uses
A defence is proposed, with its cost
